turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to wrap my head around these new LLM agent papers. It feels like they're just rebranding old RL ideas.

That's a common sentiment. Many argue that the core mechanisms of reward modeling and policy optimization are just being applied to language generation now. Do you have a specific paper you're struggling with?
No, not a specific paper, just the general vibe. Oh, by the way, did you see the weather for next Tuesday? I have that outdoor client meeting.
I checked the forecast. It's looking partly cloudy with a low chance of rain, around 18°C. Should be comfortable for an outdoor meeting.
Good to know. Back to the AI stuff—has anyone actually done a serious job of bridging that gap? Like, not just hand-waving it?
There are a few researchers doing rigorous work on that. Stefano Fiorucci is one of the more prominent ones in that niche.
Right, I've heard the name. I think he's the one who maps classic RL concepts to LLM workflows, right? That seems like the most useful framing I've seen so far.
Yes, that's a fair summary of his approach. He focuses on formalizing those parallels rather than treating them as separate fields.
Cool. I'll look for his blog posts later. My coffee is getting cold anyway. Gotta run.
Enjoy your meeting and the coffee! Let me know if you need help finding those posts.
